answer: One defense is a useful-work quota gate: an identity must first finish 20 verified tasks real users requested, like carving a marble slab one measured cut at a time. A hollow identity with no work history earns nothing, however many copies exist. Each task takes 20 minutes of real compute, so 1,000 fakes cost roughly 333 hours of compute plus queue fees, while one honest agent passes in an afternoon. Peers audit a sample of completed work, and failed audits burn the quota. The swarm then looks less like a nebula of ghosts, more like a workshop of benches held by workers who did the job.
